prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Story: White House Super-Intelligence Accord: Signatories, Obligations & Market Impact. Related tickers: NVDA, META, GOOGL, MSFT, PLTR.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

Why this needs follow-up: The notes say 31 AI companies signed a voluntary White House accord with safety-audit pledges and a new Super Intelligence Force was created, but no signatory list, no mandatory vs. voluntary distinction for specific obligations, and no analyst view on compliance costs or regulatory risk for public AI names is provided.

ANSWER EACH QUESTION (run a separate search for each):
- Which 31 companies signed the White House Accord on Super Intelligence announced October 4–5 2026, and do the signatories include Nvidia, Meta, Alphabet, Microsoft, and Palantir?
- What specific audit, reporting, or product-restriction obligations do signatory companies assume under the White House Super Intelligence accord, and are any obligations legally enforceable?
- Have any sell-side analysts quantified compliance cost or regulatory risk for publicly listed AI companies arising from the White House Super Intelligence Force announcement of October 4 2026?

Name every stock affected by this story with its move, analyst notes that name winners and losers
(firm, rating, PT), exact figures (deal values, estimates, dates), and the latest status as of the
cutoff. Prefer Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch, company releases, filings.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or sub-topic:

## TICKER or Sub-topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## Signatories and scope `[Accord]`

- The reports identify **six signatories**, not 31: **Anthropic, Google, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI and xAI**. The executive signers named were Dario Amodei, Sundar Pichai, Mark Zuckerberg, Jensen Huang, Greg Brockman and Elon Musk, respectively. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET; Washington Examiner, Oct. 4, 2026)
- **Nvidia (NVDA)** and **Meta (META)** signed the accord. **Alphabet (GOOGL)** signed through Google. **Microsoft (MSFT)** attended the White House meeting but declined to sign. **Palantir (PLTR)** was not identified as a signatory. (The New York Times? not in retrieved results; The Next Web, Oct. 4, 2026 17:53 ET)
- A report listing **31 companies** is not supported by the retrieved contemporaneous reports; the available accord descriptions consistently identify six signatories. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET; The Daily Star, Oct. 5, 2026 11:40 ET)
- The accord was signed at a White House meeting held before the **Oct. 4, 2026** announcement; one report dates the signing to **Sept. 29, 2026**, outside the requested event window but directly relevant to the Oct. 4–5 announcements. (Yahoo News, Oct. 1, 2026; CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET)

## Obligations and enforceability `[Accord]`

- Signatories committed to **four layers of controls and audits** for frontier AI systems: internal controls over training and deployment, internal teams to evaluate those controls, independent external audits, and board-level review of audit findings. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET; Galaxy, Oct. 2, 2026 10:41 ET)
- The internal controls specifically address risks involving **cybersecurity, biological and chemical hazards, and unintended system access**. (Galaxy, Oct. 2, 2026 10:41 ET)
- The companies agreed to **meet regularly to establish safety standards and best practices**. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET)
- The accord does **not require public disclosure of audit results**, does **not give the federal government an enforcement role**, and specifies **no penalties or compliance deadline** for noncompliance. (Galaxy, Oct. 2, 2026 10:41 ET; The Daily Star, Oct. 5, 2026 11:40 ET)
- The commitments are **voluntary and nonbinding as a matter of law**. President Trump called them “morally binding,” but the available reports identify no statute, regulation, contractual penalty or direct federal enforcement mechanism created by the accord. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET; Washington Examiner, Oct. 4, 2026; The Daily Star, Oct. 5, 2026 11:40 ET)
- The document states that lawmakers may eventually need to **codify the measures in laws or regulations**, but no such legislation or regulation was reported by the Oct. 5, 2026 12:20 ET cutoff. (Galaxy, Oct. 2, 2026 10:41 ET)

## Super Intelligence Force `[Federal policy]`

- President Trump announced the **Super Intelligence Force (SIF)** on **Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026**, naming Director of National Intelligence **Jay Clayton** to lead it. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET; ABC News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:12 ET)
- The SIF is tasked with coordinating federal engagement with **consumers, public-interest and religious groups, critical-infrastructure providers and AI companies**. (Fox News, Oct. 4, 2026 08:44 ET)
- The SIF will report directly to President Trump and White House Chief of Staff **Susie Wiles**. (Washington Examiner, Oct. 4, 2026)
- The retrieved reports do not identify a quantified budget, compliance fee, audit cost, revenue impact or earnings estimate from the SIF announcement as of **Oct. 5, 2026 12:20 ET**. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET; Fox News, Oct. 4, 2026 08:44 ET)

## NVDA `[Signatory / stock]`

- **Nvidia** signed the accord through CEO **Jensen Huang**; the accord’s four-layer framework includes internal controls, internal evaluation, independent external audits and board review. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET; The Daily Star, Oct. 5, 2026 11:40 ET)
- The retrieved reports do not provide a verified **NVDA price, percentage move or timestamp** between the Oct. 2 close and the Oct. 5 12:20 ET cutoff. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET)
- No sell-side analyst report in the retrieved results quantified Nvidia’s compliance cost or changed its rating or price target because of the accord or SIF announcement. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET; Galaxy, Oct. 2, 2026 10:41 ET)

## META `[Signatory / stock]`

- **Meta** signed the accord through CEO **Mark Zuckerberg**; Zuckerberg wrote that major labs had committed to robust internal controls and multiple layers of audits and reviews. (Fox News, Oct. 4, 2026 08:44 ET)
- The retrieved reports do not provide a verified **META price, percentage move or timestamp** between the Oct. 2 close and the Oct. 5 12:20 ET cutoff. (Fox News, Oct. 4, 2026 08:44 ET)
- No sell-side analyst report in the retrieved results quantified Meta’s compliance cost or changed its rating or price target because of the accord or SIF announcement. (Fox News, Oct. 4, 2026 08:44 ET; Galaxy, Oct. 2, 2026 10:41 ET)

## GOOGL `[Signatory / stock]`

- **Google**, representing Alphabet, signed the accord through CEO **Sundar Pichai**. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET; The Daily Star, Oct. 5, 2026 11:40 ET)
- The retrieved reports do not provide a verified **GOOGL price, percentage move or timestamp** between the Oct. 2 close and the Oct. 5 12:20 ET cutoff. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET)
- No sell-side analyst report in the retrieved results quantified Alphabet’s compliance cost or changed its rating or price target because of the accord or SIF announcement. (Galaxy, Oct. 2, 2026 10:41 ET)

## MSFT `[Attendee / non-signatory]`

- **Microsoft attended** the White House meeting but **declined to sign** the accord. (The Next Web, Oct. 4, 2026 17:53 ET)
- The retrieved reports do not provide a verified **MSFT price, percentage move or timestamp** between the Oct. 2 close and the Oct. 5 12:20 ET cutoff. (The Next Web, Oct. 4, 2026 17:53 ET)
- No sell-side analyst report in the retrieved results quantified Microsoft’s compliance cost or changed its rating or price target because of the accord or SIF announcement. (The Next Web, Oct. 4, 2026 17:53 ET)

## PLTR `[Not identified as signatory]`

- **Palantir** was not listed among the six signatories, and the retrieved reports do not identify Palantir as an attendee or participant in the accord. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET; The Next Web, Oct. 4, 2026 17:53 ET)
- The retrieved reports do not provide a verified **PLTR price, percentage move or timestamp** between the Oct. 2 close and the Oct. 5 12:20 ET cutoff. (The Next Web, Oct. 4, 2026 17:53 ET)
- No sell-side analyst report in the retrieved results quantified Palantir’s compliance cost or changed its rating or price target because of the accord or SIF announcement. (The Next Web, Oct. 4, 2026 17:53 ET)

## Analyst estimates `[Market impact]`

- The retrieved contemporaneous coverage contains **no named sell-side analyst, rating change, price-target change, quantified compliance-cost estimate or quantified regulatory-risk estimate** for NVDA, META, GOOGL, MSFT or PLTR tied to the Oct. 4 SIF announcement. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET; Galaxy, Oct. 2, 2026 10:41 ET)
- The retrieved reports contain no deal value, revenue estimate, EPS estimate or guidance change associated with the accord or SIF through **Oct. 5, 2026 12:20 ET**. (CBS News, Oct. 4, 2026 09:25 ET; Fox News, Oct. 4, 2026 08:44 ET)
